Europe PMC search API, resultType=core, pageSize=20; first 20 titles/abstracts (or all when fewer) screened for six listed missing-step queries; coltsfoot photoreceptor/phytochrome/phototropism query returned 4 results. Replaced OpenAlex missing steps after its round-wide HTTP 429.
General web searches with the listed Tussilago/coltsfoot queries and Asteraceae photoreceptor review; Wikipedia, ResearchGate and commercial summaries were not opened as evidence.

Full thesis inspected: Whatley 1984, https://pearl.plymouth.ac.uk/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1052&context=bms-theses . The only Tussilago occurrence is in general discussion (printed p.212; PDF p.255), citing Grime et al. 1981; Tussilago was not one of this thesis’s measured experimental taxa. The old handle 10026.1/2442 redirects to a missing migrated page, so the institution’s indexed thesis listing was followed to the legal PDF.

Family-review results inspected; full texts via Europe PMC XML PMC13413876 (10.3390/metabo16070479, light-regulated medicinal plant metabolism) and PMC12988820 (10.1111/tpj.70789, molecular plant VOC perception) contain no Tussilago or coltsfoot entry. Neither provides a species-level chemical-sensing measurement.

Screened chemical results are principally phytochemical composition, extract activity in animal cells, ethnobotany, and endophytic colonization surveys. These do not measure Tussilago reception of a chemical signal. Eye-query results concern medicine, other organisms, and image-recognition tools rather than a Tussilago eye.
Canon evidence checked for Tussilago: no entry in the logged in-hand Animal Eyes compilation; plant chemical/light canon sources are not yet in hand. Canon completion is not claimed.

The chloroplast-response paper 10.1093/plphys/kiag739 and its legal preprint 10.1101/2023.10.24.563792 are positive light-sensing leads on wanted, not evidence read. No null sense_light_nonvisual record is written while that lead awaits full text.
